issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the existence or lawfulness of a compromise underlying a decree must be decided by the court that recorded the compromise, rather than through a separate suit.
material_facts: A trial court had entered a decree in favour of the appellant, and that decree was set aside by the High Court on the basis of an alleged compromise.
The appellant denied signing or authorising the compromise petition and alleged that it was forged and fraudulent.
The appellant filed a separate suit to set aside the compromise decree; the plaint was rejected as barred, after which the High Court directed him to pursue that suit.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in directing the appellant to pursue a separate suit. The appeals were allowed, the High Court’s orders were set aside, and the matter was remitted for it to decide the applications to set aside the compromise decree in accordance with law, without expressing any view on their merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXIII Rule 3 CPC, when one party alleges and the other denies an adjustment or satisfaction by a lawful compromise, the court before which the dispute is raised must decide it. Under the Rule’s Explanation, an agreement void or voidable under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 is not lawful for this purpose. Order XXIII Rule 3A bars a separate suit to set aside a decree on the ground that its underlying compromise was not lawful; therefore, the court that recorded the decree must determine the challenge. Pushpa Devi Bhagat v. Rajinder Singh (2006) 5 SCC 566 states that the remedy is to approach the court that recorded the compromise and establish that there was no valid compromise. Banwari Lal v. Chando Devi (1993) 1 SCC 581 recognises that a party may challenge a compromise through the procedure under Order XXIII Rule 3 or in an appeal under Section 96(1), read with Order XLIII Rule 1A CPC.

predicates.proceeding_challenges_compromise_decree: A party is seeking to set aside a decree said to have been based on a compromise.
predicates.compromise_existence_or_lawfulness_dispu: A party disputes that the compromise existed or alleges a defect that makes it unlawful.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to set aside a compromise decree and disputes the compromise’s existence or lawfulness, the court that recorded the decree must decide the challenge.
